title: Young's Inequality and its Equality Case, from Weighted AM–GM

problemStatement.plain: Mathlib has Young's inequality a·b ≤ aᵖ/p + bᵍ/q for Hölder-conjugate exponents p, q and nonnegative a, b, but not its equality case. Prove that equality holds if and only if aᵖ = bᵍ, by recognizing Young's inequality as the two-term weighted AM–GM inequality (weights 1/p, 1/q on data aᵖ, bᵍ) and inheriting the equality characterization from the parent entry.

knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: jensen-inequality-oq-01-oq-01

## Problem Understanding

Add the equality case of Young's inequality (missing from Mathlib) by recognizing Young's inequality as two-term weighted AM–GM and inheriting the parent's equality characterization.

## Insights

With weights 1/p, 1/q and data aᵖ, bᵍ, the weighted geometric mean (aᵖ)^{1/p}·(bᵍ)^{1/q} collapses to a·b and the weighted arithmetic mean is aᵖ/p + bᵍ/q. The two-variable weighted AM–GM equality case (parent's weighted_amgm_eq_iff over Fin 2) then gives equality iff aᵖ = bᵍ. Hölder conjugacy 1/p+1/q=1 is the 'weights sum to 1' hypothesis.

## Dead Ends

None — the build succeeded after removing one unused simp argument.
